name: linux-arm64-kvm-validation-order-v1
purpose: Run the rejected-input validation-order checker across every exact ARM64 and generic KVM C command context, then compare the sole finding with the candidate fixed source.

artifact_identity.raw_artifact_policy: The multi-megabyte report, one-entry databases, and per-file logs were retained only under /tmp and are not repository artifacts.

finding.diagnostic: input-derived validation may return -EINVAL after vcpu may have been modified
finding.source_behavior: The external-abort path calls commit_pending_events(vcpu) before two SError validations can reject the same request.
finding.disposition: matches the existing exact-source vCPU-events atomicity candidate

complete_source_differential.eva_cross_check: The separately tracked full-source harness proves that baseline rejection changes PC, PSTATE, and the commit marker, while the fixed complete source preserves all three.

checker_policy.state_role: a pointer formal with a direct write in the typed translation unit, possibly propagated through a defined direct-call chain
checker_policy.input_role: a distinct pointer formal with no mutation proved by that summary
checker_policy.request_dependence: propagated through assignments, local initializers, and direct call results
checker_policy.rejection: an immediate -EINVAL return branch, including Frama-C's normalized result-assignment and goto form
checker_policy.deduplication: at most one diagnostic per function
excluded_effects: KVM kvm_vm_bugged and kvm_vm_dead fail-stop state

positive: state write propagated through a defined callee
silent: same object used for state and condition
cleanup error unrelated to request data
indirect rejection through a result variable

candidate_disposition.status: automated exact-source finding with vulnerable-fail/fixed-pass ARM64 KVM runtime confirmation; maintainer confirmation pending
candidate_disposition.confirmation_scope: runtime confirmed under QEMU TCG, not maintainer confirmed or upstream accepted

limitations: A behaviorally read-only pointer is only a candidate input object; the checker does not prove userspace provenance.
Mutation through opaque or indirect calls, pointer aliases, output parameters, callbacks, and assembly is not inferred.
Request dependence is variable-level and does not model memory aliases or control dependence.
Only immediate -EINVAL branches are reported; cleanup paths and other errno values are deliberately out of scope.
A zero result means this narrow source pattern was absent, not that a translation unit is correct or atomic.
The runtime control uses QEMU TCG rather than physical ARM64 hardware.
The sole finding still requires upstream KVM maintainer review.
interpretation: The checker generalizes the custom vCPU-events assertion into an AST-wide rule and isolates the same bug as the only report across all 83 exact KVM command contexts. The independent Eva state differential predicts the mutation, and the focused vulnerable-fail/fixed-pass KVM selftest confirms it at runtime under emulated ARM64 EL2. It is not yet maintainer confirmed or upstream accepted.
